commercialDecision.lockedMeaning: These are the intended commercial choices. They are not a claim that the implementation, contracts, regions, registry, or SLA evidence is complete.

hardGateReceipts.meaning: Every hard gate above has exactly one receipt in receiptsPath. A receipt may only record a closed decision with a named owner, a bound Release Candidate/effective version, an immutable evidence path with a matching SHA-256, an independent reviewer and a recorded date. While the gate is open the receipt carries no evidence path and no hash, and this file alone cannot close it.

policy.hardBlockerMeans: No sale, production release, or investor claim may rely on an open hard item.
nonWaivableClasses: unapproved legal, privacy, licensing, or pricing claim

claimPatterns.reason: Launch or time-to-value promise requires an approved RC and customer evidence.
Universal or comprehensive coverage is not claimable before the supported-platform matrix and independent tests pass.
Real-time latency requires a measured SLI, workload envelope, sample size, and Release Candidate evidence.
Automatic action claims require an enabled, tested, reversible policy and customer-visible limitation.
Compliance and certification statements require counsel-approved scope and independent attestation; roadmap text is not evidence.
Dataset size and quality claims require a signed, non-empty dataset hash and fixture results from the installed consumer.
Privacy claims require field-level payload assertions, outbound-domain inventory, retention, region, and DPA approval.
Readiness is a signed release decision, not a source or build property.
Turkish form of CLM-BANNED-LAUNCH ("dakikalar içinde devreye"): a time-to-value promise requires an approved RC and customer evidence.

Turkish form of CLM-BANNED-SCOPE ("tüm ajanlar", "tamamen desteklenir", "kapsamlı güvenlik platformu"): universal coverage is not claimable before the supported-platform matrix and independent tests pass.
Turkish form of CLM-BANNED-REALTIME ("gerçek zamanlı"): real-time latency requires a measured SLI, workload envelope, sample size, and Release Candidate evidence.
Turkish form of CLM-BANNED-AUTOMATIC ("otomatik müdahale", "otomatik karantina"): automatic action claims require an enabled, tested, reversible policy and customer-visible limitation.

Turkish form of CLM-BANNED-COMPLIANCE ("KVKK uyumlu", "SOC 2 sertifikalı"; also KVKK, which the English pattern does not name): compliance and certification statements require counsel-approved scope and independent attestation.
Turkish form of the zero-false-positive part of CLM-BANNED-AIG-DATA ("sıfır yanlış pozitif"): quality claims require a measured benign-workload benchmark on the installed consumer.
Turkish form of CLM-BANNED-PRIVACY ("verileriniz asla dışarı çıkmaz"): privacy claims require field-level payload assertions, outbound-domain inventory, retention, region, and DPA approval.
Turkish form of CLM-BANNED-READINESS ("üretime hazır", "satışa hazır", "kurumsal sınıf"): readiness is a signed release decision, not a source or build property.

hardGates.requirement: Direct-GA scope includes every advertised connector: Claude Code, Cursor, VS Code, OpenClaw, OpenCode and Codex CLI (Product decision 2026-10-11 added Codex; deploy/native/support-matrix.json soldConnectorScope). The direct-GA scope is a target, not acceptance. Codex keeps its documented host limits on every surface that sells it: the host fails open on a crashing or untrusted hook (the connector maps ask and its own errors to an explicit deny), there is no output-side interception, and the packaged hook matcher covers Bash and apply_patch only. Each connector has a supported-host matrix, signed artifact, private-registry install path, real-host E2E, rollback, support owner, and limitations.
hardGates.automatedCheck: expected connector manifest, package consumer tests, real-host E2E and claim-check

hardGates.requirement: Every investor-facing technical, customer, security, compliance, traction, and financial metric has a formula, denominator, source, Release Candidate/environment, observation window, owner, reviewer, and limitation/confidence statement.
All customer, investor, procurement, landing, README, plugin, and sales claims are mapped to the Claim Registry; only approved, unexpired claims appear on release-facing surfaces.
